newsitem.title: UK: Saudi charges British nurses with murder.
newsitem.headline: Saudi charges British nurses with murder.

text.p: Two British nurses working in Saudi Arabia have been formally charged with the murder of an Australian colleague, the Saudi embassy in London said on Tuesday.
The two women, who have not been named, had been held for questioning over the murder of nurse Yvonne Gilford, 55, at the King Fahd Military Medical Complex in Dhahran.

"They are going to meet with a representative of the British embassy later in the day," the Saudi embassy said in a statement. "There will be a trial which will examine the case in detail...The Saudi government will ensure justice for all concerned."
The case almost caused a diplomatic crisis when Saudi officials at first refused requests from British diplomats to visit the two nurses in custody in Dhahran.

But the London Foreign Office said Saudi authorities had finally agreed to a request by local embassy staff to visit the two women, who have been held since Friday. The agreement follows 48 hours of intense diplomatic pressure.

Saudi authorities are reported to have confiscated the passports of another 40 British nationals in connection with the murder investigation, raising fears that they would not be allowed to return home to Britain for Christmas.
Gilford's body was found in her room on December 11. She had been stabbed four times, battered with a hammer and smothered.
Human rights groups have expressed concern over the detention of the two women, who could face public beheading if they are convicted of murder.
